title: caragana microphylla var. buriatica
intro: Caragana microphylla var. buriatica, commonly known as a type of shrub or small tree within the pea family (Fabaceae), is native to the mountainous regions of Eastern Siberia and the Russian Far East. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include its antiseptic, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, making it effective in treating wounds, infections, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Caragana microphylla var. buriatica include its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce fever, and act as a mild diuretic. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
